questions.question: The maximum speed limit on a rural interstate highway may be:

options.text: 65 mph.
75 mph.
80 mph.
Any of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any of the above.
questions.explanation: Speed limits on rural interstate highways can be 65, 70, 75, or 80 mph. The limit varies by location. Always follow the posted speed limit where you are driving.

questions.question: A driver under 18 years old may have passengers in their car when:

options.text: They obtain their license.
They have had their license for six months.
They reach the age of 17.
Traveling to or from school.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have had their license for six months.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 18 cannot have passengers (except immediate family) until they have held their license for six months. This rule does not apply to farm work or emergencies.

questions.question: If a train is close or moving fast enough to be dangerous, you must:

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
Cross the tracks at your own risk.
Find an alternative route across tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains before crossing railroad tracks. If a train is close or going fast enough to be dangerous, do not cross. This applies even if there are no signals or if signals are broken.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn.
Wave your arms.
Use your emergency lights.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound your horn.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who might not see you. For example, if another driver is about to hit you, sound your horn.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working. You should:

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
Slam on your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: When power steering fails, you need extra force to steer. Slow down and pull off the road to a safe place to stop.

questions.question: An oncoming car is to your left and a bicyclist is to your right. You should:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Split the difference.
Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you face multiple hazards, handle one at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then you can safely pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights or a siren, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using lights or a siren. Drive to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before stopping on the right.

questions.question: When following a vehicle at night, dim your lights when you are within ____ of the vehicle.

options.text: 100 feet
200 feet
300 feet
500 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 300 feet
questions.explanation: At night, switch to low beam headlights when you are 300 feet or closer to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Highway changes ahead and to the right.
Hiking trails ahead and to the right.
Hotel ahead and to the right.
Hospital ahead and to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hospital ahead and to the right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that a hospital with emergency services is located to the right.

questions.question: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when you must react to other drivers' unexpected moves.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.correctAnswerText: TRUE
questions.explanation: Higher speeds require longer stopping distances. The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop when reacting to other drivers' unexpected moves.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look directly into the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: If you look into oncoming headlights, your eyes will tighten. After the vehicle passes, your eyes need time to adjust back to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see the road clearly.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on the shoulder of a freeway?

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to look at a map for directions.
Only if you have an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if you have an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except when there is an emergency.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to park.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral right away and press the brake pedal firmly. When safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Some traffic signals show arrows to control turns from specific lanes. What does a green arrow mean?

options.text: It is used only on one-way streets.
It means you may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
You may proceed only if the green arrow is with a circular green light.
It points the way to an airport.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means you may go, but you must turn in the direction the arrow points.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you may go, just like a regular green light. But you must turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.question: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slowly and carefully.
Do not use your high beam headlights.
Use low beam headlights to see the road better.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Fog makes it hard to see other vehicles, pedestrians, and traffic signals. When driving in fog, drive slowly and carefully. Do not use high beams. Use low beams instead, as they work better in fog.

questions.question: A "Merging lanes" sign means drivers should be ready to change lanes or let other traffic merge in.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: A "Merging lanes" sign means two lanes of traffic going the same way will soon become one lane. Be ready to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge into your lane.

questions.question: You can pass on a two-lane road with a single solid yellow line on your side of the center.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a busy intersection and cannot see around the oncoming traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for another driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as soon as the traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and the turn is safe.

questions.question: What will help a person recover from drinking alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will allow a person to recover from the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: When you see an accident, you should:

options.text: Focus on your own driving.
Keep moving.
Stop only if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived yet.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Only stop at an accident if you are involved or emergency help has not arrived. Focus on driving and keep moving. Watch for people on or near the road. Do not stop just to look at accidents, fires, or other disasters.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not brake suddenly during a blowout. Grip the steering wheel firmly to stay in your lane. Release the accelerator and slow down gradually. Once very slow, apply the brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When can you honk your horn?

options.text: When you need to stop quickly.
When passing another car.
When you lose control of your car.
When passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you lose control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time before you need to slow down.
You should slow to 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. The new speed limit begins at the sign where it is posted.
